rationale_overall: This week's pool skewed heavily toward noise: youth/school robotics tournaments (White Pine Robotics, FIRST LEGO League, Indonesia coding push), volcanic-ash satellite advisories, an unrelated WWI-munition human-interest story, illiquid foreign junior miners (Nexus Uranium, Aura Energy - ASX), a thinly-traded satellite-IoT microcap (WISeKey), private/non-investable entities (SpaceX/xAI merger - no public ticker despite the $1.25T valuation headline; Anthropic; Egypt's state defense unveiling), and geopolitical items with no attributable US-listed name (Iran/Oman nuclear talks, Agni-3 test, Cambodia port visit). The one genuine catalyst - Quantum Computing Inc (QUBT) closing a $110M acquisition of Luminar Semiconductor - is real buildup evidence for the quantum wave, but it's a single small-cap event without confirming follow-through, and no current holding (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR) showed a fundamental thesis breach this week (Rocket Lab's potential loss of a Mars Sample Return contract via Congress is a risk flag but not a breach given RKLB's broader launch cadence and separate bullish coverage; Nvidia's denial of a $100B OpenAI commitment is a clarification, not a breakdown). Absent a clearly stronger displacement case, holding the current watchlist unchanged is the disciplined weekly call.
